ai.title: terminal tool prompt fixes ampersand escaping
ai.summary: Added rule 9 to `backend/src/tools.ts` instructing the model to write raw `&` instead of `&`. Clarified that `cd` does not persist between commands in the notes section. Internal prompt adjustment only.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to run a command in the terminal, it no longer writes `&` instead of `&`. The internal instructions told the model to write `&` directly, which fixes commands like `cd backend && npm typecheck` that previously failed because of the escaped ampersand. This is already live today for anyone using the terminal tool.

ai.title: Remove 🃏 emoji from CLI greeting
ai.summary: Stripped the 🃏 emoji from the welcome message in `npm-app/src/menu.ts`. The greeting now ends with 'What would you like to do?' without the trailing icon. Scope limited to the CLI `displayGreeting` function.

eli5.text: When you open the command-line assistant, the welcome message no longer includes the playing-card emoji at the end. You will simply see 'Welcome! What would you like to do?' instead of that text followed by the 🃏 icon. This is a minor visual tweak that only affects the greeting shown in the terminal.

ai.title: checkQuota reads Stripe period for active subs
ai.summary: AuthenticatedQuotaManager.checkQuota now fetches current_period_start/end from Stripe via getCurrentSubscription when subscription_active and stripe_customer_id are set, replacing the static next_quota_reset - 1 month calculation. Falls back to next_quota_reset with console.warn if Stripe reports non-active status. Covers common/src/billing/quota-manager.ts, common/src/util/stripe.ts, and web/src/lib/stripe-utils.ts. getCurrentSubscription moved to common/src/util/stripe.ts; web/src/app/api/stripe/subscription/route.ts imports from common instead of stripe-utils.

eli5.text: When Stripe reports a subscription as active it now reads the current subscription period (start and end dates) instead of estimating a reset one month after the previously stored date. If Stripe does not report the subscription as active, the system falls back to the old estimated date and logs a warning. Paid subscribers should now see their usage window reflect the actual dates of their Stripe subscription; free users and logged-out visitors are unaffected. Live today.

ai.title: Remove unused startDate from quota check result
ai.summary: Dropped startDate from CheckQuotaResult type and AnonymousQuotaManager/AuthenticatedQuotaManager return objects in common/src/billing/quota-manager.ts. Field was unused and removed to clean up quota response shape. Internal change only.

eli5.text: A behind-the-scenes cleanup removed a date field that the billing system was tracking but never actually using to decide anything. If you looked at the internal data the program checks when someone runs out of credits, that earlier billing-period start date is no longer there, but it doesn't change how the limit is calculated or enforced. The change is already live and you wouldn't notice any difference unless you were reading the raw system responses.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.201
ai.summary: Package version updated from 1.0.200 to 1.0.201 in npm-app/package.json. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The app's version number was bumped from 1.0.200 to 1.0.201, which by itself does nothing, you won't see or feel a difference from the change on its own. This version label also packages together a set of smaller updates that were made around the same time, including fixes to how the assistant formats replies in the terminal, the removal of a joker emoji from the startup message, and improvements to checks for your usage and billing limits. If you're a subscriber, the quota checks now read your Stripe billing period so warnings about hitting limits match the dates on your actual paid plan.

ai.title: CLI shows usage limit warnings
ai.summary: npm-app/src/client.ts calls showUsageWarning() on every usage response. Removed referralLink from common/src/actions.ts UsageReponseSchema. Added returnControlToUser() in backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts and client.ts. Ensures CLI displays limit warnings immediately.

eli5.text: When you hit your monthly usage limit, the CLI now shows a warning immediately instead of waiting until the tool is finished running, and it hands control back to you right away so you can review or stop your session. You'll see the limit message appear right after the usage info comes back, regardless of whether you're on a free plan or a paid one. If you've exceeded your quota on a paid plan, you'll get a heads-up that overage charges will apply but you can keep going.

ai.title: Add Hackathon April 2025 page
ai.summary: New web route at /hackathon-april-2025 renders event details and prize tiers for Codebuff Hackathon @ Mox. Uses Next.js App Router page.tsx with client-side components. Scope limited to web/src/app/hackathon-april-2025/page.tsx. Page includes hardcoded metadata for date, location, and prizes.

eli5.text: A new event page has been added to the website that displays details for the upcoming Codebuff Hackathon at Mox in San Francisco on April 13th, 2025. The page shows the event schedule, location, and prize tiers including monthly Codebuff credits for the top three winners. Anyone visiting the site can now navigate to this dedicated page to view all the information about the hackathon, though registration details are noted as upcoming.

ai.title: Fix nested gitignore pattern resolution
ai.summary: parseGitignore now accepts projectRoot to correctly resolve relative ignore patterns. Logic updated to trim lines, handle negations, and prefix rooted patterns with the relative directory path. This ensures nested ignore files apply rules relative to their location rather than treating them as absolute or global. Affects common/src/project-file-tree.ts and npm-app/src/project-files.ts.

eli5.text: When you open a project on your computer, the assistant now correctly respects ignore rules written inside any folder, not just the main one. Previously, a rule in a subfolder's ignore file was treated as if it applied to the whole project from the top, so files that should have been skipped could still show up. The assistant now reads each ignore file relative to its own location and handles rules like 'ignore this' versus 'never ignore this' the way the file intended. You don't need to do anything differently; the fix just prevents stray files from appearing in results.
